notes: Meta Muse Wonder launch (2026-10-12) headline table: 14 benchmarks x 5 columns (Muse Wonder Full, Muse Wonder, Claude Fable 5.1, GPT-6 Astra, Claude Opus 5.5) parsed in code from the rendered dev.meta.ai model page and diffed cell by cell (74 numeric cells; OSWorld V2.1 carries a partial and a binary value per column; Claude Opus 5.5 binary is a dash). The same table appears as an image in the model card (page 3) and the blog; the image was read visually and matches every cell. Effort: every column is labelled (max) and the model card states results use max reasoning effort, except Muse Wonder Full SWE-Marathon (xhigh). Meta's selection rule (model card section 3): where a comparable third-party or provider-reported result exists Meta uses it, otherwise the highest of its internally validated run, a self-reported score or the official leaderboard score; competitor runs are best-effort and not necessarily tuned. All columns are labelled max reasoning effort except Muse Wonder Full on SWE-Marathon (xhigh). Blog-only charts with printed value labels (FocusBench and five safety charts) and the blog's Artificial Analysis index roster chart are stored with their own comparability_group. The blog bar charts for PSI, Harvey LAB-AA, Vals Finance Agent V2, AutomationBench-AA, DeepSWE, SWE-Marathon and MemoryBench repeat the table values and are not stored twice. Muse Spark rows in the AA chart: Muse Spark 1.2 and 1.1 are third_party_board_only registry entries. Meta Muse Wonder is preview per Meta docs (see models.json); Muse Wonder Full has no API. Conflicts with other sources: Meta's AutomationBench-AA (strict pass@1: Full 45.4, Wonder 39.1) is a different reading from the AutomationBench-AA index component that Artificial Analysis reports (Full 71%, Wonder 68%); Meta's GDP.pdf Opus 5.5 value (30.6, Surge) differs from the catalog's AA board reading (26.2 at max). Artificial Analysis's index values (56, 52) match Meta's table. Third-party confirmation of Meta's numbers is provisional: recheck boards (AA, Vals, DeepSWE, tbench.ai, SWE-Marathon/Abundant AI) by 2026-10-20.

claims.statement: Meta's launch table (dev.meta.ai model page, model card page 3, blog) compares Muse Wonder Full, Muse Wonder, Claude Fable 5.1, GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5, all labelled max reasoning effort except Muse Wonder Full on SWE-Marathon (xhigh). In Meta's table Muse Wonder Full tops PSI, Harvey LAB-AA, Vals Finance Agent V2, AutomationBench-AA, DeepSWE 1.1 and SWE-Marathon; Claude Opus 5.5 tops HealthBench Pro, JobBench, OSWorld V2.1 (partial), Terminal-Bench 4.0-AA, ProgramBench and the AA Index; Claude Fable 5.1 tops OSWorld V2.1 (binary); GPT-6 Astra tops GDP.pdf; Muse Wonder tops MemoryBench.
claims.implication: Vendor-published, best-of-available-source selection (internal runs, self-reports, third-party boards mixed), with different harnesses per row. Use as a lead, not a ranking. No Muse column beats Claude Opus 5.5 in Meta's own table on Terminal-Bench 4.0-AA, ProgramBench or the AA index.

claims.statement: Meta says Muse Wonder Full 'tops agentic and coding benchmarks, including DeepSWE and SWE-Marathon in independent third-party runs'. In the table the DeepSWE 1.1 gap is 79.0 (Full) vs 78.8 (Wonder) vs 74.2 (Claude Opus 5.5) vs 74.1 (GPT-6 Astra); on SWE-Marathon Full is 57.5 at xhigh, Wonder 53.1 at max, Claude Opus 5.5 46.3, Claude Fable 5.1 45.6, GPT-6 Astra 42.5.
claims.implication: The DeepSWE lead over Muse Wonder is 0.2 points with no interval published; SWE-Marathon compares vendor harnesses (Codex for Astra, Claude Code for Fable 5.1) and Full ran at xhigh, so the 'at xhigh' number says Full does not need max there.

claims.statement: In Meta's table Muse Wonder (max) trails Muse Wonder Full (max) on 14 of 15 numeric rows, by 0.2 points (DeepSWE 1.1) to 9.0 points (ProgramBench); it leads only on MemoryBench (85.6 vs 85.5). The SWE-Marathon gap (4.4) compares Full at xhigh with Wonder at max.
claims.implication: Computed from the Meta table; Full is not API-dispatchable, so the usable comparison for routing is Muse Wonder against other API models.
